title: Ethiopia Blue Nile Headwaters drought — 2021-2022
brief_outcome_free: Blue Nile headwaters around Lake Tana (Amhara). Rain-fed agriculture in the headwaters of the Blue Nile; below-normal rains threaten cropping and downstream water. You are the DOC drought analyst.

act1_quiz.prompt: Which seasonal rainfall sequence drives drought risk for rain-fed agriculture in the Blue Nile headwaters around Lake Tana?
act1_quiz.hint: The northern Ethiopian highlands have two cropping rains.
options: The belg (Feb-May) rains followed by the main kiremt (Jun-Sep) rains - a poor belg followed by a weak kiremt compounds into a failed meher harvest
Mediterranean winter rainfall arriving from the north
The coastal Bahri season of the Red Sea lowlands
act1_quiz.correct: The belg (Feb-May) rains followed by the main kiremt (Jun-Sep) rains - a poor belg followed by a weak kiremt compounds into a failed meher harvest
act1_quiz.answer_note: The northern highlands depend on the belg (Feb-May) rains and the main kiremt (Jun-Sep) rains that feed the meher harvest. If the belg under-performs, soils and households enter the kiremt already stressed, so a delayed or weak kiremt on top compounds the risk.
act1_quiz.bn_purpose: Seasonal-calendar context for when the forecast-deficit signal matters and why consecutive-season evidence compounds in the BN.

act1_quiz.prompt: Beyond local rain-fed farms, why does a rainfall deficit in the Lake Tana / Blue Nile headwaters carry wider significance?
act1_quiz.hint: Think about what this basin feeds downstream.
options: The basin is the headwaters of the Blue Nile (Abbay), so a persistent deficit depresses Lake Tana levels and downstream river flows that many users depend on
The area is Ethiopia's main seaport corridor
It is the only irrigated zone in the country
Rainfall there controls Indian Ocean cyclone activity
act1_quiz.correct: The basin is the headwaters of the Blue Nile (Abbay), so a persistent deficit depresses Lake Tana levels and downstream river flows that many users depend on
act1_quiz.answer_note: The Lake Tana basin and the surrounding highlands form the headwaters of the Blue Nile (Abbay). A sustained rainfall deficit therefore threatens both local rain-fed cropping and the lake levels and river flows on which downstream water users depend.
act1_quiz.bn_purpose: Exposure context: the spatial-coverage evidence matters because a deficit in this basin propagates to hydrological systems beyond the admin1.

decision.checkpoint_prompt: Forecast deficit and CDI agree months ahead of the event window. This is a STRONG, early signal. What DOC level do you set, and what anticipatory action does the ~6-month lead justify?

counterfactual.prompt: What if anticipatory action (agricultural input support and water-resource contingency planning) were triggered at the lead round on the strong forecast signal?
counterfactual.narrative: Slow-onset droughts give long lead. The counterfactual shows the loss-reduction value of acting on a confident seasonal signal rather than waiting for impact confirmation.
